original_question: Let beta_k=e^{sqrt(k)}/k!. The paper reports that the degree-n Jensen polynomials associated with {beta_k} have only real zeros for 1<=n<=30. Does that reality property continue for all degrees?
target_in_paper: The nearest paper-faithful target is the Section 3.1 conjecture, supported by Example 3 and later restated in Section 5, Problem 5(a): whether the s=1/2 sequence {√k/k!}_{k=0}^∞ is a classical multiplier sequence, equivalently whether φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2 belongs to the Laguerre–Pólya class with nonnegative coefficients.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly focuses on the key finite-degree evidence discussed by the paper: real-rootedness of tested Jensen polynomials and the question of whether that persists for all degrees. It also aims at the sharp, local issue in the paper rather than a broader generalization.
missing_details: The paper’s s=1/2 target sequence is {√k/k!}_{k=0}^∞, not {e^{√k}/k!}_{k=0}^∞. The draft appears to conflate the main Section 3.1 conjecture with a different nearby exponential-in-√k discussion.
The relevant entire function in the conjecture is φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ (√k/k!)(x^k/k!)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2, and the conjecture is that φ∈L-P^+.
The Jensen polynomials must be defined explicitly: for a sequence T={γ_k}_{k=0}^∞, g_n(x)=∑_{k=0}^n binom(n,k)γ_k x^k.
The quantifier should be explicit: for every n∈N_0 (or every n≥0), not just ‘for all degrees’.
The paper’s formal open problem later asks whether {√k/k!} is a multiplier sequence (Problem 5(a)); that is the official formulation nearest to the conjecture.
By Theorem 2, multiplier-sequence status is equivalent to all Jensen polynomials being hyperbolic; with these positive coefficients, this means all zeros are real and in fact nonpositive.
The ambient setting is the real Laguerre–Pólya theory: real sequences, real polynomials, and the class L-P^+ of real entire functions with nonnegative Taylor coefficients.
The paper separately asks in Problem 5(b) whether the same sequence is a CZDS; your draft omits this, which is fine if the aim is to stay narrowly with the Jensen-polynomial question.
refined_question: Is the real entire function φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2 a member of the Laguerre–Pólya class L-P^+?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is the sequence {√k/k!}_{k=0}^∞ a classical multiplier sequence; that is, for every n∈N_0, does the nth Jensen polynomial g_n(x)=∑_{k=0}^n binom(n,k)(√k/k!)x^k have only real zeros?
justification: The draft’s core idea—extrapolating from tested Jensen polynomials to all degrees—matches the evidence used by the paper for the special case s=1/2. But the draft names the wrong sequence. In Section 3.1 the authors explicitly conjecture that φ(x)=∑ √k x^k/(k!)^2 lies in L-P^+, and Example 3 says that for s=1/2 all tested Jensen polynomials had only real zeros, contrasting with the failure for s=1/20. In Section 5 they formalize the same issue as Problem 5(a): determine whether {√k/k!} is a multiplier sequence. Theorem 2 and Definition 5 supply the exact equivalence between that multiplier-sequence question and the real-rootedness of every Jensen polynomial, so the refined question above is the narrowest stand-alone version faithful to the paper’s actual intent.
